{"notes":"Mark 2026-11-22: the net serves ALL THREE purposes — an interop test federation, a directory of providers, and public onboarding where a person gets an account.

Availability re-checked by registry RDAP on 2026-11-22 (404 = free): mimi.exchange, interop.chat, mimifed.org, openmimi.net, mimi.directory, joinmimi.org and mimiinterop.org are all still free. Premium pricing not checked.

RECOMMENDATION: mimi.exchange. It names the function (providers exchanging messages), so it covers the federation and the directory; it is short enough to be a front door; and 'exchange' is a service noun rather than an institutional one, so it does not read as the standards body. Runner-up openmimi.net, where 'open' signals non-official and .net suits a network, but it is longer and reads a little activist. Rejected: interop.chat is right for the test federation but wrong for onboarding, since nobody 'joins interop'; mimi.directory names one of the three purposes only; joinmimi.org reads the most official of all, which is the thing to avoid.

THE NEUTRALITY RISK IS NOT SOLVED BY THE NAME, and this is the part worth carrying forward. With a directory and public onboarding, it is the FUNCTION that reads as official: a place to look up MIMI providers and get a MIMI account is what a reader takes for the working group's own, whatever the domain says. mimid's own rule (the reference-not-only memory) is to stay visibly separate so WG feedback is not read as steering MIMI toward Mark's product. So the mitigation is editorial, not DNS: the site says plainly and prominently that it is Mark Atwood's, not the IETF MIMI working group's, and links to the actual WG. Worth deciding that wording when the site is built, not after someone complains.

NEXT, and Mark's own action: registering is his (I cannot buy a domain). After that, DNS and DNSSEC setup with his OK, through joumon at Epik as the notes say. A subdomain of reviewcommit.com remains the free stopgap for the January interop day if he would rather not register yet."}
